name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)

lead: Mebolazine (dimethazine) is an oral anabolic steroid once sold as a medicine (Dostalon, Roxilon) and later withdrawn. From about 2008 it reappeared in gray-market supplements marketed to bodybuilders for lean mass and a fuller physique.

It is a 17α-alkylated DHT derivative and an unusual dimer of methasterone, reportedly acting as a prodrug of methasterone, an androgen receptor agonist. No clinical trials were found; published research is limited to metabolism studies.

paras: It has appeared as an oral ingredient, sometimes unlisted, in supplement products used in bodybuilding.
The FDA has taken legal action against makers of supplements containing it, and it is classed with the hepatotoxic oral steroids. Human safety data are absent.

angle.text: Mebolazine is used for lean mass gains and a fuller physique: it is reportedly converted to methasterone, which activates androgen receptors and drives muscle protein gain. It turned up in gray-market supplements; no human studies exist.

lead: Mebolazine, also called dimethazine or dymethazine, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and an unusual dimer of methasterone, two units joined by an azine group [1]. People who seek it are after the usual outcome of anabolic steroids: more lean muscle mass and a larger, harder-looking physique.

Wikipedia reports that it reportedly acts as a prodrug of methasterone and that it was once marketed as the medicines Dostalon and Roxilon but is no longer sold [1]. Since about 2008 it has been found as an unlisted ingredient in some dietary supplements, and the US FDA has taken legal action against manufacturers of such products [1]. Case reports describe it as one of the designer steroids found in a product sold as a supplement, Super DMZ Rx 2.0 [2].
No clinical trials of its effects on muscle were found. The literature consists of metabolism studies and case reports of adverse events linked to supplements that contained it [1][2][3].
infobox: Withdrawn drug; found as undeclared supplement ingredient [1][3]

paras: It is classified as an androgen receptor agonist and is reported to act as a prodrug of methasterone [1]. A 2016 study examined its metabolism in vitro and in vivo [1].

Wikipedia notes use since 2008 as an illegal ingredient in dietary supplements, including some sold as vitamin B products, with FDA legal action against makers [1]. A 2015 review in Andrology discussed the growing presence of designer androgens in over-the-counter supplements [1].

A 2023 Steroids paper analysed about 16 New York residents who reported fatigue, hair loss and muscle aches between 2012 and 2013, including one hospitalised with liver damage; testing of the implicated B-50 supplements found methasterone, dimethazine and methylstenbolone, and symptoms of severe virilization were reported in a child [3]. Wikipedia more broadly reports that a 2007 to 2016 analysis found 776 supplements with unlisted pharmaceutical ingredients, including muscle-building products contaminated with anabolic steroids [4].

A 2014 case report in the Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports described what the authors called the first case of cholestatic jaundice linked to Super DMZ Rx 2.0, a product containing methylstenbolone and dymethazine. The patient was a previously healthy 26-year-old man who took the product as directed for 30 days, and the authors noted that such supplements may hide potent androgens from consumers [2]. A 2024 review of 50 years of case reports on anabolic-androgenic steroid abuse found methylstenbolone most strongly linked to hepatic complications [3]. Wikipedia categorises mebolazine among hepatotoxins [1].
No studies found testing mebolazine as a treatment or performance aid in people. Published human data are limited to case reports of harm from supplements that contained it [2][3].

timeline.event: Begins to appear as an undeclared ingredient in dietary supplements [1].
Reports of liver and other symptoms in New York residents using B-50 supplements containing dimethazine and other steroids [3].
Case report of cholestatic jaundice with a supplement containing dymethazine and methylstenbolone [2].
